Designed by Eduardo Ruiz

Homemade, like a good flan.

Flan is an original open-source wireless split keyboard in four sizes, with interchangeable cases and flush magnetic display frames.

Support Flan on Ko-fi ↗
36keys in Flan36
2wireless halves
4case styles

An original design

The keyboard and its CAD are designed by Eduardo Ruiz. It is inspired by Piantor by beekeeb and keeps its 36 key positions and angles; the PCBs, case, frames and firmware are original.

Keycap meshes and some component models come from credited third-party libraries.

Build status & dimensions

Routed digital prototype. PCB DRC, ERC and schematic parity checks pass. Physical assembly and hardware operation still need validation.

Electronics bay
mm
Frame roof
mm
Plate height
mm

Heights above the base, without feet. Magnetic frames, printed threads, cables and contacts require physical tests. Component models combine library CAD and nominal reconstructions.

Component models & dimensions↗Stack & frame construction↗Source repository↗

Credits & licenses

Original keyboard & CAD
Designed by Eduardo Ruiz. Inspired by Piantor by beekeeb, whose 36 key positions and angles it keeps (GPL-3.0); the PCBs, case outline, cases, frames and firmware are original. Flan36 is not affiliated with beekeeb.
KLP Lamé keycaps
braindefender · CC-BY-SA-4.0. Original meshes, placed and colored. Pinned source ↗
Component models
KiSwitch Choc v1 · MIT. KiCad library models · CC-BY-SA-4.0 with library exception. Per-file sources & changes ↗
Viewer libraries
Three.js 0.180.0, fflate and meshoptimizer 1.2.0 · MIT.
